definition: Candidate missing connections in the first map or inspected material, not proven absent ideas or abandoned work.

items.title: The EXACT / QUANTIZED / DERIVABLE ladder
items.seed: S22 distinguishes storing an exact object, retaining an approximation, and retaining a recipe that can reconstruct it. It also explicitly withholds support for the cited GVA mechanism.
items.missing_bridge: The first dossier mapped cache policies but did not give this three-way action space its own research object. A valid reconstruction contract is still needed for each object type.
items.why_keep: The useful question is what can be regenerated cheaply and verifiably. That question survives failure of the claimed KV mechanism or its citation.
items.next_bridge: Start with an object that is actually reproducible, such as a parser index from immutable source bytes. Record recipe, inputs, versions, reconstruction cost and the equivalence check. Do not assume a value tensor determines its discarded key tensor.
items.attribution_scope: The cited passage contains the precursor; this does not establish adoption, correctness or priority.
items.change_mind: An existing evaluated implementation closes this mapping gap; or reconstruction loses required information or costs more than keeping the object.
items.absence_scope: Underconnected in the first dossier or unresolved in inspected passages; not proven absent from the entire corpus or live system.

items.title: Dormancy without declaring an idea dead
items.seed: The notes contain adaptive TTL proposals, a preservation metaphor, cold storage, expiration, retraction and resurrection conditions.
items.missing_bridge: A cache eviction, an expired observation, a rejected claim and a promising unused idea need different reasons and return conditions. These distinctions were compressed into separate memory and retraction sections.
items.why_keep: Low recent use does not by itself establish low future value. Keeping a cheap pointer can preserve an option without consuming active context.
items.next_bridge: Separate storage residency, permission/freshness and evidential standing. A dormant hypothesis may return after a new task; a retracted assertion needs new evidence, not mere renewed demand.
items.attribution_scope: The cited passage contains the precursor; this does not establish adoption, correctness or priority.
items.change_mind: A current state schema already distinguishes these cases and delayed-use tests demonstrate correct restoration; or the added distinctions do not improve retrieval or error control.
items.absence_scope: Underconnected in the first dossier or unresolved in inspected passages; not proven absent from the entire corpus or live system.

items.title: Reports that name the decision they could change
items.seed: S18 proposes decision-linked reporting with a decision ID, deadline and owner. S28 proposes routing according to stakes, cost and user preference.
items.missing_bridge: The first map emphasized compute scheduling more than the operator’s limited review capacity. The actual reporting filter and its misses have not been demonstrated by these passages.
items.why_keep: An unattended loop can still generate more adjudication work than it saves. Decision relevance offers a concrete target beyond reducing notification count.
items.next_bridge: Compare a plain queue with decision-linked grouping. Audit both escalated and demoted reports; allow an unclassified urgent event to bypass the filter.
items.attribution_scope: The cited passage contains the precursor; this does not establish adoption, correctness or priority.
items.change_mind: Matched runs show no reduction in review time, delayed important decisions, or alarms lost because they did not fit an existing decision ID.
items.absence_scope: Underconnected in the first dossier or unresolved in inspected passages; not proven absent from the entire corpus or live system.

items.title: A place for evidence the current schema cannot express
items.seed: S18 attacks vocabulary capture, schema smuggling and the conversion of critique into more familiar types.
items.missing_bridge: Typed admissibility can make an idea disappear before it is assessed. The map needs a way to distinguish malformed data from a challenge to the map itself.
items.why_keep: This protects potentially useful surprises, including objections to this dossier’s categories. Novelty does not have to contradict an invariant or attract disagreement to be useful.
items.next_bridge: Retain an untyped observation with source, uncertainty and a question; give it no execution authority. Later map it, amend the schema, or park it with a reason.
items.attribution_scope: The cited passage contains the precursor; this does not establish adoption, correctness or priority.
items.change_mind: All planted out-of-schema but relevant observations survive ordinary intake equally well, or the extra channel produces burden without recoverable value.
items.absence_scope: Underconnected in the first dossier or unresolved in inspected passages; not proven absent from the entire corpus or live system.

items.title: Competing historical reconstructions as separate playable variants
items.seed: The corpus advocates preserving multiple reconstructions, parameterized mechanics, cultural context and attribution. Its particular historical assertions still require specialist sources.
items.missing_bridge: A passing game engine proves consistency with selected rules; it does not decide which reconstruction is historically warranted. That provenance layer deserves its own map.
items.why_keep: A rules dispute can become a useful branching dataset rather than a forced synthesis that silently invents a canonical past.
items.next_bridge: Separate the attested source, reconstructed rule, implementer choice and generated presentation. Run each coherent ruleset under its own identifier; record which moves distinguish the variants.
items.attribution_scope: The cited passage contains the precursor; this does not establish adoption, correctness or priority.
items.change_mind: Reliable historical evidence resolves a variant, or the implementation already retains these layers without conflation.
items.absence_scope: Underconnected in the first dossier or unresolved in inspected passages; not proven absent from the entire corpus or live system.

items.title: A stochastic organ contract for physical computing
items.seed: S31 distinguishes a device that samples a distribution from one that preserves a deterministic value. The model atlas already represents distributions, coverage and runtime costs.
items.missing_bridge: The physical branch was largely summarized as a warning about energy claims. Its positive connection to the atlas’s measurement contract was underdeveloped.
items.why_keep: A common description of task, output distribution, tolerance, calibration and total cost could make unlike compute surfaces comparable for a bounded job.
items.next_bridge: Specify one sampling task and a digital reference before choosing a device. Include encoding, readout, calibration and repeated samples in the cost boundary.
items.attribution_scope: The cited passage contains the precursor; this does not establish adoption, correctness or priority.
items.change_mind: No useful task contract spans the candidate substrates, or interface and calibration costs erase any advantage. A simulation alone does not settle physical performance.
items.absence_scope: Underconnected in the first dossier or unresolved in inspected passages; not proven absent from the entire corpus or live system.

items.title: Sovereignty as recoverable human choice
items.seed: The Sovereign Mirror includes user override; S18 explores exit and fork rights. These express a design aim, not a validated score.
items.missing_bridge: The first map asks about offline capability and burden, but ability to understand, disagree, export and continue elsewhere needs explicit observations.
items.why_keep: A system might finish more tasks while making its operator less able to repair or leave it. The aspiration is meaningful before a composite metric exists.
items.next_bridge: Use separate transfer, correction and restart exercises. Measure whether the operator can carry a task to a clean environment, reject a recommendation and recover state without the original assistant.
items.attribution_scope: The cited passage contains the precursor; this does not establish adoption, correctness or priority.
items.change_mind: Observed exit and correction performance fails to improve, or the selected tasks do not reflect what the operator means by sovereignty.
items.absence_scope: Underconnected in the first dossier or unresolved in inspected passages; not proven absent from the entire corpus or live system.

items.title: When a behavioral passport stops being informative
items.seed: The atlas stores uncertainty and coverage; the migration critique versions model, tokenizer, template and mapper separately.
items.missing_bridge: A passport needs a rule for when measurements become stale or fail to transfer. Age alone and a model name alone are inadequate proxies.
items.why_keep: The passport can become a record of what remains unknown and which small probe would most improve routing, rather than a static label.
items.next_bridge: Invalidate affected predictions after declared runtime changes; compare scheduled probes with error-triggered probes on held-out routing jobs.
items.attribution_scope: The cited passage contains the precursor; this does not establish adoption, correctness or priority.
items.change_mind: Selective reprobes cost more than their routing benefit, or routine fixed probes provide equal protection and accuracy.

items.title: Metadata as a fallible forecast of future relevance
items.seed: S24 identifies unknown future queries as the central difference from scene rendering and proposes span, path, entity and hash metadata.
items.missing_bridge: The source also calls these bounds deterministic. Their extraction can be deterministic while their completeness for future semantic questions remains uncertain.
items.why_keep: Treating retrieval bounds as a forecast produces a testable engineering problem without discarding the rendering analogy.
items.next_bridge: Create future queries that use a different name, omit a path, or depend on an old negation. Compare exact metadata triggers, semantic retrieval and a broader fallback.
items.attribution_scope: The cited passage contains the precursor; this does not establish adoption, correctness or priority.
items.change_mind: The bounded task class admits complete rules with no missed necessary spans, or the predictive metadata fails to beat a simpler search baseline.

items.title: Preserve why an idea failed without banning its return
items.seed: S19 gives tombstones a justification and resurrection condition; S05 values dormant variants.
items.missing_bridge: The system needs to distinguish a refuted mechanism from a failed implementation, a bad operating regime, and a merely unaffordable experiment.
items.why_keep: An old failure can prevent repeated waste, but a vague tombstone can also suppress a useful idea after assumptions change.
items.next_bridge: Store failure scope and dependencies, the retained residue of the idea, and the observation that would reopen it. Test both false resurrection and wrongful suppression.
items.attribution_scope: The cited passage contains the precursor; this does not establish adoption, correctness or priority.
items.change_mind: A simpler archive already supports these decisions, or recorded failure reasons do not help new readers distinguish changed conditions from repetition.
items.absence_scope: Underconnected in the first dossier or unresolved in inspected passages; not proven absent from the entire corpus or live system.

items.title: The basis metaphor’s useful residue: who rescues which failures?
items.seed: The rank/basis proposal asks for capability directions instead of more intensity; the coordination critique distinguishes shared prior from genuinely new observations.
items.missing_bridge: The general linear-algebra theorem is unsupported, but the question of complementary task failures is concrete and was underrepresented beside that criticism.
items.why_keep: A weaker overall model or a new sensor may be valuable on the particular jobs the current fleet misses.
items.next_bridge: Measure conditional rescue on held-out failure cases, charge the extra calls, and test whether the selector can identify when to use the specialist. Use no assumption of linearity or independence.
items.attribution_scope: The cited passage contains the precursor; this does not establish adoption, correctness or priority.
items.change_mind: Rescues disappear outside the selection set, a same-model extra attempt performs as well, or routing cannot recognize the cases in advance.

items.title: The history of idea selection, not just the history of claims
items.seed: The notes inspect how shared maps prime later answers and how a fold can preserve sanctioned disagreement while losing other alternatives.
items.missing_bridge: The first dossier preserves source-to-claim links better than it preserves considered-but-unselected ideas and the reasons for leaving them out.
items.why_keep: A future reader can revisit a choice intelligently only if it can distinguish rejected evidence, budget limits and editorial compression.
items.next_bridge: Version the candidate set and record selection reasons. Give a fresh reader a bounded raw-source pack before showing the synthesis, then compare recoverable mechanisms rather than lexical novelty.
items.attribution_scope: The cited passage contains the precursor; this does not establish adoption, correctness or priority.
items.change_mind: The raw-first view adds no independently checkable mechanism or exposes no material selection loss, or its benefit is outweighed by review cost.
